name: B10-0125/2026 (PPE) – Post-election situation in Uganda and threats against opposition leader Bobi Wine
title: JOINT MOTION FOR A RESOLUTION on the post-election situation in Uganda and threats against opposition leader Bobi Wine
part_text:
The European Parliament condemns Uganda's January 2026 election as fraudulent and violent, and the crackdown on the opposition. It calls for the release of detained opposition figure Kizza Besigye and everyone held over the elections. It demands that the military stop pursuing opposition leader Bobi Wine and guarantee his safety. It asks the European Union to rethink its cooperation with Uganda and consider sanctions on those responsible, and asks the International Criminal Court to investigate. The resolution is an opinion; it does not itself change any law.

- The European Union is asked to review its cooperation with Uganda and consider sanctions on named individuals.
- Uganda's government and military leaders are the target; opposition figures and missing people are the concern.
- The International Criminal Court is asked to investigate; the Parliament's position goes to the Council, Commission and Uganda's authorities.
